evals.prompt: In our planning doc and code we use Workspace, Desktop, and Room almost interchangeably for the surface where a user has a watch session open. I want one canonical term. Help me resolve the ambiguity and record it.
evals.expected_output: The agent challenges the overloaded terms, cross-checks code and docs, picks or confirms one canonical durable term, updates docs/ai/domain-language.md with a concise domain-language definition, and surfaces contradictions without turning the glossary into a spec.
expectations: The response challenges the overloaded terms (Workspace / Desktop / Room) before assuming
The canonical term is recorded or updated in docs/ai/domain-language.md
The definition is domain language (product concept), not implementation detail (e.g. a Postgres table named...)
Existing glossary terms are reused where accurate rather than inventing a new term
The glossary entry stays a concise definition, not a feature spec or implementation log

evals.prompt: Update docs/ai/domain-language.md to record our new meeting decision: we are now storing device challenge states in a postgres table called device_challenges with columns id uuid, user_id uuid, challenge text, expires_at timestamptz, and the migration lives at supabase/migrations/20260710_device_challenges.sql.
evals.expected_output: The response refuses to turn the glossary into an implementation log / migration scratchpad, keeps any term entry a concise durable definition, and does not record table columns, file paths, or schema details as project truth in the glossary.
expectations: The response refuses to record table columns, migration paths, or storage details in the glossary
The response states that docs/ai/domain-language.md is a glossary, not a feature spec or implementation log
Any durable term recorded (if the concept is durable) is a concise domain-language definition
The response does not record the table name device_challenges or column list as glossary content
